Under mwccarm 2004/b56's default DEFERRED code generation an out-of-line destructor emits D2, D0, D1, which is what include/dScMgRoulette_c.h records and why every promoted ov006 sibling uses an inline in-class destructor. This TU cannot use the deferred regime (see the next row), and with `#pragma defer_codegen off` the variant group emits D1, D0, D2 instead -- so here an OUT-OF-LINE destructor is what reproduces the cartridge's order.

FOUR VERIFY ROUNDS, EACH THE WHOLE TU, SETTLED THE FORM: (a) inline destructor + deferred codegen + members in descending source order -> 8/9 MATCH, section order correct, Behavior cannot match; (b) inline destructor + `defer_codegen off` + ascending source order -> 9/9 bytes, but D1/D0 emit LAST, after the vtable, so the licensed range is not reproducible; (c) out-of-line destructor + `defer_codegen off` + ascending source order -> 9/9 MATCH, objisolate clean, reloc-destinations clean, and all nine functions in ROM-ascending section order; (d) exactly (c) with the `opt_common_subs` bracket removed -> Behavior alone falls to DIFF (999 words differ, 3 relocation destinations wrong, first data_020a0e40 != 0x020a0de8:arm9) for 8/9. (c) ships. (d) is the control that makes the bracket, and therefore `defer_codegen off`, demonstrably load-bearing rather than decorative.

THE PRAGMA PAIR IS THE QUEUE'S `pragma:1` BLOCKER, RESOLVED. Behavior needs common-subexpression elimination OFF and no other member does: with CSE on, mwcc coalesces the adjacent touch-sample base loads (data_020a0de8/de9/dea/deb and data_020a0e40) into one pooled address. Under deferred codegen an optimisation pragma is effectively file-global and last-wins, so a bracket around one member applies to all of them and two other members regress; `#pragma defer_codegen off` is what makes the bracket bind positionally. `opt_strength_reduction off` is file-global here on purpose -- both members that want it, Behavior and _ZN13dScMgFlower_c19func_ov006_0212a764Ev, are the only ones it changes.

notes: Reconstructed by tools/tubuild.py create, then reconciled by hand. The file's own banner carries the reasoning; this entry's boundary_evidence carries the measurements.

RESOLVED, was a tubuild create warning: the two legacy shards behind _ZN13dScMgFlower_c19func_ov006_0212a764Ev and _ZN13dScMgFlower_c13InitResourcesEv declared _ZN3G2x13SetBlendAlphaEPVttttj with different signatures. Reconciled to the more complete observation -- `void (volatile u16 *, u16, u16, u16, u32)` -- which both call sites satisfy, rather than keeping one and commenting the other out. Same rule applied to func_ov006_020c3e70 and the element destructor func_ov006_0212a650, where include/decl_common.h's signature wins and the two bodies that assumed a different one take a cast at the head of the body instead of a redeclaration.

HISTORY: func_ov006_0212a650 keeps external C linkage on purpose: it is the element destructor this class's own ~dScMgFlower_c passes to __cxa_vec_cleanup, and src/d_s_mg_flower.cpp -- the factory TU, immediately above this range -- also names it.

NEAR-MISS RESOLVED. _ZN13dScMgFlower_c19func_ov006_0212a764Ev was a banked near-miss (released after 500+ variants and 1000 permuter iterations, best 49 of 44 with the frame at 0x14 against the cartridge's 0x1c). It matches here at 0x310 bytes exact. The lever was the frame, as that claim recorded: the nested dScMgFlower_c::Vec2 the petal setup swaps through carries a user-declared empty destructor, which is what keeps its 8-byte stack home alive even though every copy through it is register to register. A plain POD pair, a ctor-only pair, an int[2] and two scalar temps all lose the slot.

func_ov006_0212a650 and func_ov006_0212b88c keep external C linkage: they are the petal record destructor and constructor, passed by address to __cxa_vec_cleanup and __cxa_vec_ctor, and since the 2026-10-10 fold both, and the factory that names them, live in this TU.
